answer: Each epoch the tide auctions a fixed pool of live slots, and a kernel holding none is inert. Bidding burns nectar, and the pool never grows with demand, so every clone a sybil adds lifts the clearing price for all the rest; the thousandth kernel pays what scarcity sets rather than a per-head fee, and no batch, shard, or parallel queue splits one bid into many cheap ones. The bill is nectar at the rising clearing price, attached to each kernel that holds a slot. It fails if governance can inflate the pool or slots become tradable.
